surfaces.part: ramp slope surface with chevron texture
left cave cliff wall strip (dark, vertical face seen at the side)
flat floor apron in front of the ramp

answer.evidence: The tile is 48 px wide and 80 rows tall. Rows 0-63 are one continuous sloped ramp surface with a chevron texture. It is bounded on the left and right by dark cliff-wall strips with a dark outline, and it ends at row 63 on a dark line. Rows 64-79 are flat floor with sparse speckles. The ramp has no south-facing vertical front face of 3 or more rows. There is also no front-edge line with eave shadow, and no ellipse. The column scans at x=12, 24 and 35 show only texture noise, with no band, edge-line or face change. The tile therefore reads as a flat top-down slope with side cliff walls and no front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 7 visible tones per tile, equal to the paving reference and above the grass reference (3). Only 18% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the dark brown side edges are tinted to the material rather than a black sticker line. The chevron ramp surface shows about 5 lightness steps, with per-plank highlight and shadow lines and some grain. Near-flat coverage is 16% against 0% in both references, which comes from the smoother sandy strip at the bottom and the wider chevron bands. That strip is a small area and still carries speckle, so I don't count it as a flat fill. The piece is a little simpler than the paving reference, but a careful artist would accept it next to the references.
